summary: I'm a Full Stack Developer with hands-on experience building scalable, event-driven systems for AI-powered products. At Einstellen.AI, I've worked across 4 microservices, designing RBAC access control, async AI interview workflows, real-time WebSocket chat, and Kafka-based event-driven architecture, while also building the React/TypeScript frontend. I enjoy solving backend and system design problems: things like idempotent message processing, distributed rate limiting, and PostgreSQL performance tuning. I'm now diving into GenAI to build AI-driven applications, and this assistant itself is one of those projects, a live demo of how I combine full-stack engineering with AI.

experience.description: AI-driven hiring platform built using Django and a microservices architecture.

Designed a feature-level access-control (RBAC) system across Django microservices and React/TypeScript frontend, using Redis-cached, fail-closed authorization checks for consistent, low-latency permission handling.

Built reusable UI components in TypeScript and React, and used Redux Toolkit (RTK) for state management across the frontend.
Added real-time chat using WebSockets for bi-directional communication between users on the platform.
Used Apache Kafka to decouple microservices through an event-driven architecture, improving scalability and fault isolation.
Improved PostgreSQL performance for large, structured datasets through query tuning, indexing, and materialized views, reducing data retrieval latency.
Developed dynamic, scalable web applications using Django, HTML, and JavaScript.
Revamped interactive website features that increased user engagement by 30%.
Led cross-browser compatibility testing, achieving 95% usability consistency across devices.

projects.name: Multi-Channel Notification Fan-Out System
projects.description: An event-driven notification system that fans out a single business event (e.g., 'order shipped') to Email, SMS, and Push channels via Kafka topics and independent Celery workers.
projects.problem_solved: Ensures one channel's failure doesn't block the others when delivering notifications across multiple channels.
key_features: Used Redis distributed locks and database-level unique constraints to keep message processing idempotent, avoiding duplicate sends under Kafka's at-least-once delivery guarantees.
Added a retry mechanism with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue for failed deliveries, so provider outages don't affect the rest of the pipeline.
Built a PostgreSQL schema with a materialized view tracking per-channel delivery success rates for real-time visibility into notification health.

projects.name: RAG_Chat_App
projects.description: A full-stack RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) chatbot that answers company-specific questions using a custom knowledge base, with a Django REST backend and a React frontend.
projects.problem_solved: Demonstrates how to ground an LLM's answers in real documents instead of general knowledge, with citations back to the source and a measurable way to test answer accuracy.
projects.your_role: Solo builder — designed and built the full stack, from the ingestion and retrieval pipeline to the chat UI and the evaluation system.
key_features: RAG pipeline that chunks and embeds a document knowledge base into a Chroma vector store, retrieves relevant context per question, and answers using an LLM.
A 30-question evaluation dataset with LLM-as-judge scoring, checking both retrieval accuracy and answer correctness across categories.
A Gradio dashboard to run the evaluation and view accuracy broken down by document category.

faqs.question: Why should we hire you?
faqs.answer: I believe I'm a strong fit for development roles. I'm self-motivated and put my full effort into whatever I'm working on — that's what helped me do well academically, and it's the same mindset I bring to real projects. At Einstellen.AI, I've owned backend design across multiple microservices, built event-driven systems with Kafka, and worked on everything from access control to real-time features — both as an individual contributor and as part of a team. That mix of technical depth and adaptability is what I'd bring to any team I join.
